# Adjudication Task — Chapter 337

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃337화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|넓고 차가운 전각 안. 창틈 사이를 비집고 들어온 외풍(外風)에 창가에 놓인 호롱불이 흔들린다. 그 위로 어느 노인의 얼굴이 천천히 겹쳐졌다.
  6|
  7|녹광이 스며든 두 눈동자와 고목처럼 마른 몸.
  8|
  9|노인의 이름은 당사독. 별호는 만독수라.
 10|
 11|천하 오대세가의 일원인 사천당가의 가주이자, 얼마 전 아버지를 잃은 한 사람의 아들이다.
 12|
 13|휘이이잉.
 14|
 15|닫힌 창을 두드리는 찬 바람 소리에는 몇 시진 전 들었던 그의 목소리가 묻어 나오는 듯했다.
 16|
 17|
 18|
 19|‘소식을 들었을 때는 모든 것이 늦은 후였다. 사지가 온전한 곳이 없더군.’
 20|
 21|
 22|
 23|일신(一神), 삼성(三星), 십왕(十王).
 24|
 25|한때 십만 마도에 맞서 천하를 구해 낸 영웅들은 이미 호호백발 노인이 된 지 오래였다.
 26|
 27|누군가는 늙거나 병들어 죽고, 누군가는 평온을 찾아 자취를 감추고, 후사를 맡긴 뒤 자리에서 물러나기도 했다.
 28|
 29|독왕(毒王) 당사문도 자신의 길을 찾아 떠났다.
 30|
 31|
 32|
 33|‘이틀 거리에 미산(眉山)이라는 곳이 있다. 아버님께서는 종종 미산의 아름다운 산세에 대해 말씀하시곤 하셨지.’
 34|
 35|
 36|
 37|이십여 년 전, 가주직에서 물러난 독왕이 미산으로 향한 것은 어쩌면 당연한 일이었다.
 38|
 39|그곳은 한평생 무림의 거센 물살을 이겨 낸 노 무림인이 선택한 마지막 안식처였으리라.
 40|
 41|
 42|
 43|‘찾아오는 걸 달갑지 않게 생각하셨다. 드물게 한 번씩 사람을 보내 확인하는 것으로 대신할 수밖에 없었어.’
 44|
 45|
 46|
 47|그리고 그건 평생 지워지지 않을 흉터가 되었다.
 48|
 49|지금으로부터 며칠 전, 믿기 힘든 급보가 전해진 것이다.
 50|
 51|혼비백산하여 달려간 당사독이 목격한 것은 경천동지할 전투의 흔적과 독왕의 시신이었다.
 52|
 53|
 54|
 55|‘아버님의 시신은…… 심각하게 훼손되어 있었다. 그건 틀림없는 고문의 흔적이었지.’
 56|
 57|
 58|
 59|흉수(兇手)가 무슨 이유로 독왕을 고문했는지는 모른다.
 60|
 61|그러나 한 시대를 풍미했던 초절정 고수, 독왕 당사문은 그렇게 죽었다. 이름도 얼굴도 모르는 미지의 인물에 의해.
 62|
 63|분기탱천한 당사독이 직접 가솔들을 이끌고 주위를 샅샅이 뒤졌지만 이미 늦은 후였다.
 64|
 65|
 66|
 67|‘반드시 놈을 찾아내어 죽일 것이다. 사지를 갈가리 찢어 구주(九州)에 뿌리고, 놈의 몸뚱어리에서 흘러나온 피를 사해오호(四海五湖)로 흘려보낼 것이다.’
 68|
 69|
 70|
 71|숨 막히는 살기를 흘리며 분노하는 당사독에게 무슨 말을 할 수 있을까. 나는 그의 분노와 다짐을 충분히 이해했다.
 72|
 73|그와 사천당문은 흉수를 잡아 죽일 때까지 결코 멈추지 않을 것이다. 신의를 찾는 것에 도움을 줄 수 없는 것은 당연한 일이었다.
 74|
 75|“독왕 당사문이 죽었다. 바로 그 독왕이…….”
 76|
 77|거대한 지각변동이 일어나고 있다. 그것도 아주 가까이에서.
 78|
 79|내가 호롱불을 바라보며 나직하게 중얼거린 그때, 등 뒤에서 다급한 목소리가 들려왔다.
 80|
 81|“입조심 좀 해라. 사천당문 한복판에서 그런 말을 하면 어떻게 되는지 몰라?”
 82|
 83|목소리의 주인이 누구인지 알아차리는 건 그리 어려운 일이 아니었다. 이미 다가오는 세 사람의 기척을 진즉 알아차린 지 오래였으니까.
 84|
 85|나는 고개도 돌리지 않고 대답했다.
 86|
 87|“왔냐.”
 88|
 89|“왔냐가 아니라, 입조심을 하라고. 입!”
 90|
 91|“괜찮아. 근처에 아무도 없으니까.”
 92|
 93|“조심 좀 하자는 얘기다. 네놈이랑 있다 보면 살 떨려서 이거 원.”
 94|
 95|궁기방이 한숨을 내쉬며 의자에 털썩 주저앉았다. 뒤따라 들어온 청풍, 혁무진도 각자 한 자리씩을 차지했다.
 96|
 97|“어디 다녀오는 길이야?”
 98|
 99|궁기방이 퉁명스럽게 대답했다.
100|
101|“개방 성도 분타.”
102|
103|“문경이도 같이?”
104|
105|“그럴 리가. 당문에서 따로 내어준 전각에 틀어박혀 있다. 아까 보니 약방문에 푹 빠져서 누가 들어온 줄도 모르더라. 하룻밤 묵고 내일 같이 떠날 듯싶다.”
106|
107|“그래서, 알아낸 건 있고?”
108|
109|“아니, 헛수고야. 사천당문에 관해서 넌지시 찔러 봤더니 분타주도 아직 잘 모르고 있더군.”
110|
111|그럴 만도 하다. 들었던 바에 의하면 독왕의 거처는 아무도 찾지 않는 심산유곡에 마련되어 있었고, 당사독이 보낸 식솔이 비밀리에 한 번씩 들릴 뿐이었으니까.
112|
113|‘게다가 사천당문에서 작정하고 숨겼으니…….’
114|
115|당사독은 오로지 가문의 힘으로 복수하길 원했다.
116|
117|사천당문이라는 무림 세가가 지닌 힘과 그들이 보여 준 성격을 생각해 본다면, 지금 같은 독자적인 행보가 그리 이상한 일은 아니다.
118|
119|“좀 수상쩍게 생각하긴 하더군. 근래에 사천당문에서 사람을 보내 필요한 정보를 요구했다더라고.”
120|
121|“이미 냄새 맡았네. 혹시 말했어?”
122|
123|잠시 머뭇거리던 궁기방이 입을 열었다.
124|
125|“비록 당사독 대협께서 함구령을 내리셨지만…… 나는 개방의 후개다. 분타주에게만 사실을 말해 주고 수상쩍은 놈들은 모두 감시하라고 일러두었지.”
126|
127|“청 소협은?”
128|
129|심각한 분위기 속, 하품을 참느라 안간힘을 쓰고 있던 청풍이 대답했다.
130|
131|“은인이 시키신 대로 할아버지께 전서응을 보냈어요.”
132|
133|궁기방이 고개를 끄덕이며 덧붙였다.
134|
135|“아무리 늦어도 칠 주야 안에는 소식이 갈 거다.”
136|
137|“그래, 잘했다.”
138|
139|이 정도면 최소한의 조치는 취했다고 생각한다.
140|
141|만약 당사독이 알게 된다면 분노하겠지만…… 내게는 반드시 해야 할 일이었다.
142|
143|“저어, 조장님.”
144|
145|“응?”
146|
147|혁무진이 주위의 눈치를 살피며 조심스럽게 입을 열었다.
148|
149|“뭐 하나만 여쭤봐도 됩니까?”
150|
151|“안 된다고 하면, 안 물어볼래?”
152|
153|“아뇨. 저 궁금한 건 못 참는 성격인 거 아시잖아요.”
154|
155|“…….”
156|
157|가뜩이나 심란해 죽겠는데 어이없네.
158|
159|오랜만에 확 그냥 한 대 시원하게 갈겨 줄까 하다가 참았다.
160|
161|“뭔데.”
162|
163|“왜, 왜 주먹을 쥐고 그러세요. 무섭게.”
164|
165|“그럼 뜸 들이지 말고 그냥 물어봐, 이 자식아.”
166|
167|경계의 눈빛으로 내 주먹을 바라보던 혁무진이 작게 속삭였다.
168|
169|“흉수가 누굽니까?”
170|
171|“흉수?”
172|
173|“네, 천하의 독왕 당사문 대협을 죽이고 고문하기까지 한 흉수요.”
174|
175|“허허, 흉수라.”
176|
177|빡!
178|
179|“악! 왜 때리고 그러세요!”
180|
181|“내가, 알면, 여기서, 이러고, 있겠냐. 응?”
182|
183|빡! 빡! 빡! 빡!
184|
185|참지 않고 뒤통수에 연타를 먹이자 속이 뻥 뚫리는 기분이다.
186|
187|“어으, 모르면 모른다고 하시면 되지 왜…….”
188|
189|“자식이 말 같지도 않은 소리를 하고 있어. 열 받게.”
190|
191|“쓰으읍. 흐으.”
192|
193|궁기방이 머리를 부여잡은 채 발버둥 치는 혁무진을 한심한 눈빛으로 바라보았다.
194|
195|“쯧쯧, 길거리 황구(黃狗)보다 우매한 친구로군. 그 천인공노할 놈이 어디에서 온 누구인지 어찌 알겠나?”
196|
197|혁무진이 찔끔 흘러나온 눈물을 닦으며 중얼거렸다.
198|
199|“궁 소협은 그 길거리 황구 옆에서 돗자리 펴고 구걸하시잖아요.”
200|
201|“뭣이이!”
202|
203|“왜요, 제가 틀린 말 했습니까?”
204|
205|“감히 본 방을 무시해!”
206|
207|“입은 삐뚤어져도 말은 바로 하랬다고, 오해 마십시오. 저는 궁 소협만 무시한 겁니다.”
208|
209|청풍이 깔깔 웃으며 박수를 쳤다.
210|
211|“와! 은인! 혁 소협이 궁 소협 무시했대요!”
212|
213|“웃지 말고 좀 말려! 청풍 이 미친놈아!”
214|
215|혁무진 저 자식, 말빨 많이 늘었네.
216|
217|나는 팩트 폭행으로 눈깔이 뒤집힌 궁기방을 손으로 막아서며 말했다.
218|
219|“둘 다 진정해.”
220|
221|이걸로는 효과가 없을 것 같아서 한마디 덧붙였다.
222|
223|“나한테 맞아 뒈지기 싫으면.”
224|
225|“…….”
226|
227|“…….”
228|
229|이제 좀 낫군.
230|
231|나는 서로를 향해 씨근덕거리는 녀석들을 보며 한숨을 푹 내쉬었다.
232|
233|“흉수가 어떤 놈인지 누가 알겠냐. 알았으면 사천당문 쪽에서 진작 잡아 죽였지.”
234|
235|여전히 눈에 힘을 풀지 않은 혁무진이 말했다.
236|
237|“저도 압니다. 제 말은 짐작 가는 구석이 없냐는 거죠.”
238|
239|“묻기 전에 생각을 좀 해라, 생각을. 이 우매한 녀석아.”
240|
241|“그런데 언제 봤다고 계속 반말입니까? 개방 후개라고 대태원진가의 진룡대 부대주를 무시해도 되는 겁니까? 안 그래요, 조장님?”
242|
243|……사실 그 정도 차이면 무시해도 될 것 같긴 한데.
244|
245|대답하지 않자 혁무진의 눈초리가 가늘어진다.
246|
247|나는 은근슬쩍 화제를 돌렸다.
248|
249|“뭐, 수상쩍은 놈들이야 무림에 널리고 널렸지. 당장 암천이나 마교 놈들도 있고.”
250|
251|“흥! 그뿐인 줄 아느냐?”
252|
253|거세게 콧방귀를 뀐 궁기방이 말을 받았다.
254|
255|“사천당문은 사마외도(邪魔外道)의 척결에 온 힘을 기울인 곳, 개인적인 원한이 있는 자의 소행일 수도 있다.”
256|
257|나는 궁기방의 콧잔등에 달라붙은 코딱지를 혐오스럽게 바라보며 물었다.
258|
259|“사마외도는 이미 싹 쓸어버린 거 아니었나?”
260|
261|“아무리 마당을 쓸어도 모래는 남는 법. 천하가 얼마나 넓은데 몸 숨길 곳 하나 없었을까. 끈질긴 추격에도 끝끝내 살아남은 자들이 있다.”
262|
263|그것도 일리가 있는 말이다.
264|
265|게다가 천하를 장악한 정파 무림의 추적에도 살아남았다면 하나같이 엄청난 고수임이 틀림없다.
266|
267|‘마치 소림에서 상대했던 음양쌍괴(陰陽雙怪)처럼.’
268|
269|죽은 줄 알았던 초절정의 마두 두 사람이 소림에 등장할 줄, 과연 누가 알았을까.
270|
271|무림은 수많은 은원(恩怨)의 사슬이 엉켜 있는 곳. 어디에서 무슨 일이 벌어져도 이상하지 않다.
272|
273|‘거기에 고문까지.’
274|
275|고문을 가하는 경우는 두 가지다.
276|
277|죽이기 전에 고통을 주고 싶을 만큼 원한이 있거나, 아니면 그의 입을 통해 듣고 싶은 무언가가 있거나.
278|
279|목적은 몰라도 한 가지는 확실하다.
280|
281|‘……더럽게 위험한 놈이 나타났군.’
282|
283|동시에 우연히라도 마주치고 싶지 않은 놈이다.
284|
285|현재 내 경지는 절정의 끝자락. 아직 깨달음을 얻지는 못했지만, 시스템을 통해 얻은 힘으로 초절정 초입까지는 상대할 수 있다.
286|
287|‘태을무정검 황보엄이 대표적이지.’
288|
289|하지만 그 이상의 고수라면 어렵다. 실제로 황보엄과의 전투 도중 자그마한 깨달음을 얻지 못했다면, 놈의 태을무형검에 무릎을 꿇었을지도 모른다.
290|
291|하물며 상대가 십왕(十王) 중에서도 다섯 손가락에 들던 독왕을 죽일 만큼의 고수라면…….
292|
293|‘지금으로서는 필패(必敗).’
294|
295|안타깝지만 인정할 수밖에 없는 현실이다.
296|
297|조용히 생각에 잠겨 있던 그때, 궁기방이 문득 생각났다는 듯 불쑥 입을 열었다.
298|
299|“생각해 보니 살수(殺手)일 가능성도 있군.”
300|
301|“살수? 암살자?”
302|

But Poison King Tang Taesang, a Supreme Peak master who had dominated an entire era, had died that way. At the hands of an unknown figure whose name and face remained a mystery.

[P23]
Furious beyond measure, Tang Sadok had personally led his clansmen in combing the surrounding area, but it was already too late.

[P24]
*I will find that bastard and kill him. I’ll tear his limbs apart and scatter them across the Nine Provinces, then let the blood from his body flow into the Four Seas and Five Lakes.*

[P25]
What could anyone say to Tang Sadok as he raged, radiating suffocating killing intent? I understood his anger and resolve well enough.

[P26]
He and the Sichuan Tang Clan would never stop until they found the culprit and killed him. Naturally, they could not spare anyone to help us find the Divine Physician.

[P27]
“Poison King Tang Taesang is dead. The Poison King himself…”

[P28]
A massive upheaval was taking place. And it was happening right beside us.

[P29]
Just as I murmured those words while staring at the oil lamp, an urgent voice came from behind me.

[P30]
“Watch your mouth. Do you have any idea what’ll happen if you say something like that in the middle of the Sichuan Tang Clan?”

[P31]
It was not difficult to tell who the voice belonged to. I had sensed the three of them approaching long ago.

[P32]
Without turning my head, I answered, “You’re back.”

[P33]
“Not ‘you’re back.’ I said watch your mouth. Your mouth!”

[P34]
“It’s fine. There’s no one nearby.”

[P35]
“I’m saying we should be careful. Being around you scares the life out of me.”

[P36]
Gung Gibang sighed and dropped into a chair. Cheongpung and Hyuk Mujin entered behind him and each claimed a seat.

[P37]
“Where did you go?”

[P38]
Gung Gibang answered curtly.

[P39]
“The Chengdu branch of the Beggars’ Sect.”

[P40]
“Mungyeong went with you?”

[P41]
“Of course not. He’s holed up in the pavilion the Tang Clan provided for him. When I saw him earlier, he was so absorbed in a medicinal prescription that he didn’t even notice someone had come in. He’ll probably stay the night and leave with us tomorrow.”

[P42]
“So? Did you find anything out?”

[P43]
“No. It was a waste of time. I casually probed the branch leader about the Sichuan Tang Clan, but he didn’t know much either.”

[P44]
That was understandable. From what I had heard, the Poison King’s residence lay deep in a remote mountain valley that no one ever visited. Only a member of Tang Sadok’s household would secretly stop by every once in a while.

[P45]
*Besides, the Sichuan Tang Clan deliberately covered everything up…*

[P46]
Tang Sadok wanted his family to take revenge on its own.

[P47]
Considering the power of the Sichuan Tang Clan and the temperament they had displayed, there was nothing particularly strange about them acting independently.

[P48]
“He did find it a little suspicious. Apparently, the Sichuan Tang Clan recently sent people to request some information they needed.”

[P49]
“They’ve already caught the scent. Did you tell him?”

[P50]
Gung Gibang hesitated for a moment before speaking.

[P51]
“Although Great Hero Tang Sadok ordered everyone to remain silent… I’m the Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect. I told the branch leader the truth and instructed him to keep an eye on anyone suspicious.”

[P52]
“What about Young Hero Cheongpung?”

[P53]
Amid the serious atmosphere, Cheongpung was struggling mightily to suppress a yawn.

[P54]
“I sent a messenger eagle to my grandfather, just as my Benefactor instructed.”

[P55]
Gung Gibang nodded and added, “The message will reach him within seven days at the latest.”

[P56]
“Good. Well done.”

[P57]
I thought we had taken the bare minimum of precautions.

[P58]
Tang Sadok would be furious if he found out, but this was something I had to do.

[P59]
“Um, Captain.”

[P60]
“Hmm?”

[P61]
Hyuk Mujin glanced around cautiously before speaking.

[P62]
“May I ask you something?”

[P63]
“If I say no, will you refrain from asking?”

[P64]
“No. You know I can’t stand not knowing something.”

[P65]
“……”

[P66]
I already had enough on my mind without this idiot adding to it.

[P67]
For a moment, I considered giving him a good, satisfying smack for the first time in a while, but held myself back.

[P68]
“What is it?”

[P69]
“Why are you clenching your fist? That’s scary.”

[P70]
“Stop stalling and ask, you bastard.”

[P71]
Hyuk Mujin eyed my fist warily and whispered, “Who’s the culprit?”

[P72]
“The culprit?”

[P73]
“Yes. The culprit who killed and even tortured Great Hero Tang Taesang, the Poison King.”

[P74]
“Well, well. The culprit.”

[P75]
*Smack!*

[P76]
“Argh! Why did you hit me?”

[P77]
“If I, knew, would I, be here, doing this? Huh?”

[P78]
*Smack! Smack! Smack! Smack!*

[P79]
I pummeled the back of his head without holding back. It was wonderfully cathartic.

[P80]
“Ugh… If you didn’t know, you could’ve just said so. Why…”

[P81]
“Because you’re spouting nonsense and pissing me off.”

[P82]
“Th-that’s…”

[P83]
Gung Gibang looked contemptuously at Hyuk Mujin as he thrashed around, clutching his head.

[P84]
“Tsk, tsk. What a fool. Even a stray yellow dog is wiser than you. How would anyone know who that heinous bastard is or where he came from?”

[P85]
Hyuk Mujin wiped away a stray tear and muttered, “You spread a mat beside that stray yellow dog and beg in the street.”

[P86]
“What did you say?!”

[P87]
“Why? Am I wrong?”

[P88]
“How dare you insult our Sect!”

[P89]
“They say you should call a spade a spade. Don’t misunderstand—I only look down on you, Young Hero Gung.”

[P90]
Cheongpung burst out laughing and clapped.

[P91]
“Wow! Benefactor! Young Hero Hyuk said he looks down on Young Hero Gung!”

[P92]
“Don’t laugh! Stop him, you lunatic Cheongpung!”

[P93]
Hyuk Mujin’s tongue had gotten a lot sharper.

[P94]
I held back Gung Gibang, who looked ready to explode after that brutal dose of truth.

[P95]
“Both of you, calm down.”

[P96]
That did not seem sufficient, so I added one more thing.

[P97]
“Unless you want me to beat you to death.”

[P98]
“……”

[P99]
“……”

[P100]
That was better.

[P101]
I let out a deep sigh as I watched them glower and huff at each other.

[P102]
“Who knows what kind of bastard the culprit is? If we knew, the Sichuan Tang Clan would’ve caught and killed him already.”

[P103]
Still glaring, Hyuk Mujin said, “I know that. I mean, do you have any guesses?”

[P104]
“Think before you ask. Think, you foolish bastard.”

[P105]
“But when did we become close enough for you to keep speaking informally to me? Does being the Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar give you the right to look down on the Vice Squad Leader of the great Jin Family of Taiyuan? Don’t you agree, Captain?”

[P106]
…Actually, given the difference between them, it did seem reasonable for him to look down on Mujin.

[P107]
When I did not answer, Hyuk Mujin’s eyes narrowed.

[P108]
I subtly changed the subject.

[P109]
“Well, Murim is crawling with suspicious bastards. There are the Dark Heaven and Demonic Cult bastards, for starters.”

[P110]
“Hmph! Do you think they’re the only possibilities?”

[P111]
Gung Gibang snorted and picked up the thread.

[P112]
“The Sichuan Tang Clan devoted itself to wiping out demonic and heterodox forces. It could have been someone with a personal grudge.”

[P113]
I stared in disgust at the booger stuck to the bridge of Gung Gibang’s nose.

[P114]
“Weren’t those demonic and heterodox bastards wiped out already?”

[P115]
“No matter how thoroughly you sweep a courtyard, some sand always remains. The world is vast. Do you really think there was nowhere for them to hide? Some survived to the bitter end despite the relentless pursuit.”

[P116]
That was a valid point.

[P117]
And if they had survived being hunted by the orthodox faction that ruled Murim, every last one of them had to be an incredible master.

[P118]
*Like the Yin-Yang Twin Freaks I fought at Shaolin.*

[P119]
Who could have imagined that two Supreme Peak fiends believed to be dead would appear at Shaolin?

[P120]
Murim was a place where countless chains of gratitude and grudges became tangled together. No matter what happened or where, nothing was truly surprising.

[P121]
*And there was the torture.*

[P122]
There were two reasons to torture someone.

[P123]
Either you hated them enough to make them suffer before killing them, or there was something you wanted them to tell you.

[P124]
I did not know the culprit’s purpose, but one thing was certain.

[P125]
*…One seriously dangerous bastard has appeared.*

[P126]
And he was someone I did not want to encounter, even by chance.

[P127]
My current realm was at the very edge of Peak. I had not yet attained enlightenment, but with the power I had obtained through the System, I could hold my own against someone who had just entered Supreme Peak.

[P128]
*Hwangbo Eom, the Taeeul Merciless Sword, was a perfect example.*

[P129]
But an opponent beyond that level would be difficult. In fact, if I had not gained a small insight during my battle with Hwangbo Eom, I might have fallen to his Taeeul Formless Sword.

[P130]
And if my opponent was powerful enough to kill the Poison King, who had ranked among the five strongest of the Ten Kings…

[P131]
*As I am now, defeat would be certain.*

[P132]
As much as it pained me, I had no choice but to accept that reality.

[P133]
While I was quietly lost in thought, Gung Gibang suddenly spoke as if something had just occurred to him.

[P134]
“Come to think of it, the culprit could be an assassin.”

[P135]
“A killer? An assassin?”

[P136]
“Is there some other kind?”

[P137]
I frowned.

[P138]
“You think those bastards are that skilled?”

[P139]
“You don’t know what you’re talking about. According to my Master, the Valley Master of Moonshadow Assassination Valley has killed no fewer than three Supreme Peak masters.”

[P140]
“…An assassin killed three Supreme Peak masters?”

[P141]
“Without a doubt. I heard it threw the entire Murim into an uproar.”

[P142]
“Then is that Valley Master or whatever the greatest assassin under heaven?”

[P143]
Gung Gibang looked at me as though I were the most insane person alive.

[P144]
“What are you talking about? The greatest assassin under heaven has never changed.”

[P145]
“Oh.”

[P146]
I had momentarily forgotten.

[P147]
The Sword Saint. The Bow Saint. And finally, the man known as the Slaughter Saint.

[P148]
*When I first heard the name, I thought he was called the Slaughter Saint simply because he’d killed so many people.*

[P149]
As it turned out, being an assassin was his actual profession.

[P150]
According to Jeok Cheongang, he had taken more lives than anyone could count. He killed people from the orthodox, demonic, and heterodox factions alike, so fairly and impartially that he had even been branded an enemy of all Murim.

[P151]
*That was until the Great Faction War.*

[P152]
He had killed so many demonic fiends that people had no choice but to issue an amnesty decree for the man who had once been an enemy of all Murim—and give him the alias Slaughter Saint.

[P153]
“Of course, there’s no way the Slaughter Saint killed Great Hero Tang Taesang, but the Sichuan Tang Clan is probably considering the possibility that an assassin did it.”

[P154]
“It’s unfortunate, but they’ll deal with it themselves.”

[P155]
Whoever the culprit was, I had only one goal: find the Divine Physician and save Jeok Cheongang.

[P156]
It was unfortunate that we could not receive help from the Sichuan Tang Clan, but Qingcheng and Emei still remained.

[P157]
Which meant…

[P158]
“Young Hero Gung, did you pull that booger out in advance so you could eat it as a late-night snack?”

[P159]
“What did you say?!”

[P160]
“Wahahaha! Benefactor! Young Hero Gung is going to eat his booger as a late-night snack!”

[P161]
…No, seriously. What the hell was wrong with these bastards?

[P162]
Unable to take it any longer, I overturned the table.

[P163]
“Get the hell out! We have to leave early tomorrow, so go get some damn sleep!”

[P164]
I unleashed a lion’s roar and chased the Bermuda Triangle away, then dropped back into my chair.

[P165]
I stared blankly at the flickering oil lamp before murmuring, “Inventory open. Summon.”

[P166]
*Tap.*

[P167]
A small jade-colored shard appeared in my palm.

[P168]
When I turned over the **Divine Physician’s Token**, faint writing appeared.

[P169]
> The finest Chinese gallnuts come from Sichuan.

[P170]
“Chinese gallnuts, my ass. He should’ve written down his damn address.”

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

# Translation Rules

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 337

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃337화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|넓고 차가운 전각 안. 창틈 사이를 비집고 들어온 외풍(外風)에 창가에 놓인 호롱불이 흔들린다. 그 위로 어느 노인의 얼굴이 천천히 겹쳐졌다.
  6|
  7|녹광이 스며든 두 눈동자와 고목처럼 마른 몸.
  8|
  9|노인의 이름은 당사독. 별호는 만독수라.
 10|
 11|천하 오대세가의 일원인 사천당가의 가주이자, 얼마 전 아버지를 잃은 한 사람의 아들이다.
 12|
 13|휘이이잉.
 14|
 15|닫힌 창을 두드리는 찬 바람 소리에는 몇 시진 전 들었던 그의 목소리가 묻어 나오는 듯했다.
 16|
 17|
 18|
 19|‘소식을 들었을 때는 모든 것이 늦은 후였다. 사지가 온전한 곳이 없더군.’
 20|
 21|
 22|
 23|일신(一神), 삼성(三星), 십왕(十王).
 24|
 25|한때 십만 마도에 맞서 천하를 구해 낸 영웅들은 이미 호호백발 노인이 된 지 오래였다.
 26|
 27|누군가는 늙거나 병들어 죽고, 누군가는 평온을 찾아 자취를 감추고, 후사를 맡긴 뒤 자리에서 물러나기도 했다.
 28|
 29|독왕(毒王) 당사문도 자신의 길을 찾아 떠났다.
 30|
 31|
 32|
 33|‘이틀 거리에 미산(眉山)이라는 곳이 있다. 아버님께서는 종종 미산의 아름다운 산세에 대해 말씀하시곤 하셨지.’
 34|
 35|
 36|
 37|이십여 년 전, 가주직에서 물러난 독왕이 미산으로 향한 것은 어쩌면 당연한 일이었다.
 38|
 39|그곳은 한평생 무림의 거센 물살을 이겨 낸 노 무림인이 선택한 마지막 안식처였으리라.
 40|
 41|
 42|
 43|‘찾아오는 걸 달갑지 않게 생각하셨다. 드물게 한 번씩 사람을 보내 확인하는 것으로 대신할 수밖에 없었어.’
 44|
 45|
 46|
 47|그리고 그건 평생 지워지지 않을 흉터가 되었다.
 48|
 49|지금으로부터 며칠 전, 믿기 힘든 급보가 전해진 것이다.
 50|
 51|혼비백산하여 달려간 당사독이 목격한 것은 경천동지할 전투의 흔적과 독왕의 시신이었다.
 52|
 53|
 54|
 55|‘아버님의 시신은…… 심각하게 훼손되어 있었다. 그건 틀림없는 고문의 흔적이었지.’
 56|
 57|
 58|
 59|흉수(兇手)가 무슨 이유로 독왕을 고문했는지는 모른다.
 60|
 61|그러나 한 시대를 풍미했던 초절정 고수, 독왕 당사문은 그렇게 죽었다. 이름도 얼굴도 모르는 미지의 인물에 의해.
 62|
 63|분기탱천한 당사독이 직접 가솔들을 이끌고 주위를 샅샅이 뒤졌지만 이미 늦은 후였다.
 64|
 65|
 66|
 67|‘반드시 놈을 찾아내어 죽일 것이다. 사지를 갈가리 찢어 구주(九州)에 뿌리고, 놈의 몸뚱어리에서 흘러나온 피를 사해오호(四海五湖)로 흘려보낼 것이다.’
 68|
 69|
 70|
 71|숨 막히는 살기를 흘리며 분노하는 당사독에게 무슨 말을 할 수 있을까. 나는 그의 분노와 다짐을 충분히 이해했다.
 72|
 73|그와 사천당문은 흉수를 잡아 죽일 때까지 결코 멈추지 않을 것이다. 신의를 찾는 것에 도움을 줄 수 없는 것은 당연한 일이었다.
 74|
 75|“독왕 당사문이 죽었다. 바로 그 독왕이…….”
 76|
 77|거대한 지각변동이 일어나고 있다. 그것도 아주 가까이에서.
 78|
 79|내가 호롱불을 바라보며 나직하게 중얼거린 그때, 등 뒤에서 다급한 목소리가 들려왔다.
 80|
 81|“입조심 좀 해라. 사천당문 한복판에서 그런 말을 하면 어떻게 되는지 몰라?”
 82|
 83|목소리의 주인이 누구인지 알아차리는 건 그리 어려운 일이 아니었다. 이미 다가오는 세 사람의 기척을 진즉 알아차린 지 오래였으니까.
 84|
 85|나는 고개도 돌리지 않고 대답했다.
 86|
 87|“왔냐.”
 88|
 89|“왔냐가 아니라, 입조심을 하라고. 입!”
 90|
 91|“괜찮아. 근처에 아무도 없으니까.”
 92|
 93|“조심 좀 하자는 얘기다. 네놈이랑 있다 보면 살 떨려서 이거 원.”
 94|
 95|궁기방이 한숨을 내쉬며 의자에 털썩 주저앉았다. 뒤따라 들어온 청풍, 혁무진도 각자 한 자리씩을 차지했다.
 96|
 97|“어디 다녀오는 길이야?”
 98|
 99|궁기방이 퉁명스럽게 대답했다.
100|
101|“개방 성도 분타.”
102|
103|“문경이도 같이?”
104|
105|“그럴 리가. 당문에서 따로 내어준 전각에 틀어박혀 있다. 아까 보니 약방문에 푹 빠져서 누가 들어온 줄도 모르더라. 하룻밤 묵고 내일 같이 떠날 듯싶다.”
106|
107|“그래서, 알아낸 건 있고?”
108|
109|“아니, 헛수고야. 사천당문에 관해서 넌지시 찔러 봤더니 분타주도 아직 잘 모르고 있더군.”
110|
111|그럴 만도 하다. 들었던 바에 의하면 독왕의 거처는 아무도 찾지 않는 심산유곡에 마련되어 있었고, 당사독이 보낸 식솔이 비밀리에 한 번씩 들릴 뿐이었으니까.
112|
113|‘게다가 사천당문에서 작정하고 숨겼으니…….’
114|
115|당사독은 오로지 가문의 힘으로 복수하길 원했다.
116|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

{
"chapter": 1,
"decisions": [
{
"hunk_id": "H001",

Include exactly one decision for every numbered hunk, in hunk order. `replacement` is required only for `REPAIR`.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
